home.title: ExpatRate: Know what to quote
home.description: ExpatRate tells expat job seekers what salary to quote in any country, monthly and annually, in any currency. Free, no login, transparent methodology.
home.sub: Moving countries for work? Portals ask for your expected salary in their currency. ExpatRate gives you a defensible range, a walk-away floor, and the local package structure, from public data with every source shown.
home.trust1: Your resume never leaves this device
home.footerData: A purchasing-power floor for {n} countries; verified market benchmarks for {b} destination countries. Data: World Bank PPP, national statistics offices, recruiter surveys. Rates: open.er-api.com with frankfurter.dev fallback.
home.footerAdvice: Estimates are indicative only and are not financial, tax, or legal advice.

results.floorAboveBody: The top of this market ({ceiling} per year) buys about {pct}% less than your life today. Your break-even is {floor} per year, which no local employer pays for this role. If you accept a market offer, you accept that cut knowingly; push on equity, super, and title to close part of it.

results.employerTitle: Their stated range vs your floor

results.remotePolicyLead: Your result shows two anchors. Research on real remote pay tells you which one to argue from.
results.remotePolicyLocal: Pay tracks the worker country far more than the employer country: in a 100,023-worker platform study, the worker country explained 31 percent of wage variance against 0.04 percent for the employer country.
results.remotePolicyAgnostic: Still, {pct} percent of remote workers report location-independent pay bands.
results.remotePolicyMagnitude: Where employers do adjust for location, published systems use tiers of roughly 15 to 25 percent off the HQ rate, not full localization.
results.remotePolicyAdvice: Argue from the employer-market anchor only if the role is explicitly location-agnostic or global-banded; otherwise anchor to your local market, which is where most offers land.
results.fxBody: Live exchange rates could not be fetched, so figures use the snapshot from {date}. Treat converted amounts as close, not exact.

seo.answer: The median {level} {family} salary in {country} is {median} per year, with the market band from {low} to {high} ({source}).
seo.appDescription: Free expat salary quote tool: market percentiles and a purchasing-power floor for any country, with every source shown.
seo.datasetDescription: Salary benchmarks by role family, seniority level, and country, curated from official statistics and cited recruiter sources.
seo.detailDescription: Median {family} pay in {country} with the full P25-P75 band by seniority, sources and dates shown. Get your personal quote in two minutes.
seo.monthlyNote: About {amount} per month at the median.
seo.medianOnlyNote: This level publishes a median only; no percentiles are available.
seo.ctaBody: These are market medians. Your own quote also depends on your current pay, your walk-away floor, and the package you need.
seo.countryHubAnswer: Verified market data for {n} role families in {country}. Every number cites its source. For any other country, the purchasing-power floor works everywhere.
seo.roleHubAnswer: Verified {family} benchmarks by country. Every number cites its source.
seo.methodologyH1: How every number on ExpatRate is computed
seo.methodologyMarket: The market quote takes P25, median, and P75 for your role family and seniority from official statistics and cited recruiter sources; every row lists its sources and review date. Where no verified source exists, the cell stays an explicit gap.
seo.methodologyFloor: The purchasing-power floor transfers your net salary at World Bank PPP rates and grosses it up at the target country's effective tax rate, so you know the gross needed to live as well as today.
seo.methodologyTax: Tax comes from 2026 legislated schedules where verified; 179 of 206 countries currently use a conservative 20 percent default instead, and results say so.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.description: ExpatRate privacy: no accounts, no databases, resumes never leave your device, anonymous aggregate analytics only.
privacy.intro: ExpatRate collects no personal data. There is no account, no login, and no server-side database.
privacy.deviceBody: Your resume is parsed entirely inside your browser; it is never uploaded, and no network request carries it (verified by automated test). Your wizard answers are saved only in your browser local storage, and the share link encodes them in the URL you copy.
privacy.analyticsBody: We use Cloudflare Web Analytics, which is cookie-free and reports only aggregate, anonymous page views. No consent banner is needed because no identifiers are stored.
privacy.externalBody: The page fetches live currency rates from open.er-api.com (with frankfurter.dev as fallback), and if you paste a job posting link, your browser fetches that posting directly from the job board's own public API (Greenhouse, Lever, or Ashby). Those requests carry no personal data. Those are the only third parties that receive anything.

engine.benchmarkQuality: Benchmark quality: {quality} for this role, level, and country.
engine.noBenchmark: No market benchmark for this role and country yet; only the purchasing-power floor is shown.
engine.pppStaleReason: Purchasing-power data predates the 2024 ICP round on at least one side of the move; the floor is indicative.
engine.executiveBand: Executive band: benchmarks indicate a floor, not a midpoint; ranges are wide.
engine.remoteForeign: Remote for a foreign company: two market anchors are shown, so confidence is reduced.
engine.volatileCurrency: Target currency is volatile; quote with an annual review clause and check the USD anchor.
engine.originTaxEstimate: Origin tax tier is an estimate; the floor is indicative.
engine.targetTaxDefaultReason: Target country tax is a flat 20% default (no verified tier yet); the grossed-up floor is indicative.
engine.salaryCurrencyDiff: Your salary currency {from} differs from {country}; converted at today's rate.
engine.packageOnTop: Your stated salary excludes checked package components; the floor was raised to compare like for like.
engine.healthOverlap: {country} funds healthcare from tax, which the gross-up already pays for. The health-insurance lift prices fully private cover on top, so it may overstate the floor; untick Health insurance if you would rely on the public system.
engine.targetTaxDefault: {country} has no verified tax tier yet; the floor used a flat 20% default deduction for the gross-up, so it is indicative.
engine.pppStale: Purchasing-power data for {names} predates the 2024 ICP round; treat the floor as indicative.
engine.medianOnly: Market data for this role and level publishes a median only; the band is shown at that single point.
engine.upperBand: The upper band (P75) is not published for this role and level here; the stretch is capped at the published median.
engine.floorAboveMarket: Your purchasing-power floor ({floor} per month) sits above the market ceiling ({ceiling}) for this role. The market cannot fund your current lifestyle at local rates; the quote below is the winnable market number.
engine.currencyRisk: This currency has moved sharply. Quote with an annual FX review clause or a USD-indexed component, and check the USD anchor alongside the local figure.
engine.entryMode: Entry mode: no prior salary given, so this quote comes from the market band alone. There is no purchasing-power floor to show.
